title: Prohibition of unsubstantiated generic green claims
text: Under the EU Green Claims and Empowering Consumers directives, generic environmental claims such as 'eco-friendly', 'green', or 'climate neutral' are prohibited unless the recognised excellent environmental performance relevant to the claim is proven and disclosed.

title: Verifiable basis for superlative claims
text: Superlative and 'best/No.1' claims must be based on objective, verifiable and representative data, and that basis must be disclosed to consumers.

title: Objective comparison with competitors
text: Comparative advertising must objectively compare material, relevant, verifiable and representative features, must not mislead, and must not create confusion with or discredit a competitor.

title: Prior lowest price for reductions
text: Under the Omnibus Directive, any announcement of a price reduction must indicate the prior lowest price applied by the trader during at least the 30 days before the reduction.

title: Substantiation for quantified efficacy
text: Quantified performance or efficacy claims must be substantiated, with the test method, conditions and comparison basis disclosed to the consumer.

title: Authorised health claims only
text: Health claims must be authorised and listed in the EU register of nutrition and health claims; making an unauthorised health claim is prohibited.

title: Lawful basis for data collection
text: Collecting personal data through advertising requires a clear lawful basis under the GDPR and transparent information provided to the data subject at the point of collection.
